name: Newenham Abbey
text: Your train passes through the site of Newenham Abbey, a Cistercian abbey founded in 1247 by Reginald de Mohun, a short way south-west of Axminster.

name: Forde Abbey
text: Your train passes near Forde Abbey, on the train's {side}, a Cistercian monastery whose last abbot surrendered it to the Crown in 1539; it became a house. The philosopher Jeremy Bentham rented it in 1815.

name: Church of All Saints, Sutton Bingham
text: Your train passes near the Church of All Saints at Sutton Bingham, on the train's {side}, from the 1100s and 1200s. Its wall paintings of the 1300s were whitewashed over at the Reformation.

name: Clifton Maybank House
text: Your train passes near Clifton Maybank House, on the train's {side}, a country house with Tudor work surviving. Part of it was taken away to nearby Montacute House.

name: Sherborne Abbey
text: Your train passes near Sherborne Abbey, on the train's {side}, a Saxon cathedral from 705 to 1075, then a Benedictine abbey church, and a parish church since 1539.

name: Sherborne Old Castle
text: Your train passes near the ruins of Sherborne Old Castle, on the train's {side}, built in the 1100s as the palace of Roger, Bishop of Salisbury. Walter Raleigh leased it in 1592, and Parliament's army took it after a siege in 1645.

name: Templecombe Preceptory
text: Your train passes near the site of Templecombe Preceptory, on the train's {side}, founded by the Knights Templar in 1185. A face painted on oak panels in about 1280, found in an outhouse in the village, may come from it.

name: Old Wardour Castle
text: Your train passes near the park of Wardour Castle, on the train's {side}, with the ruins of Old Wardour Castle, built in the 1390s and left uninhabitable after fighting in the Civil War in 1643 and 1644.

name: Place Farm, Tisbury
text: Your train passes near Place Farm at Tisbury, on the train's {side}, once a grange of Shaftesbury Abbey. Its medieval barn is said to be the largest in England.

name: John Halle's Hall
text: Your train passes near John Halle's Hall in Salisbury, on the train's {side}, a merchant's hall of the 1400s that is now the foyer of a cinema.

name: Borbach Chantry
text: Your train passes near Borbach Chantry at West Dean, on the train's {side}, a chapel built in about 1333. When the church it belonged to was pulled down in 1868, the chapel was kept, and it is all that remains.

name: Offa's Dyke
text: Your train passes near Offa's Dyke at Sedbury, on the train's {side}, the earthwork that roughly follows the border between England and Wales, named after Offa, king of Mercia from 757 to 796.

name: Gloucester Cathedral
text: Your train passes near Gloucester Cathedral, on the train's {side}. Edward II was buried there in 1327, and it stood in for Hogwarts in the Harry Potter films.

name: Max Gate
text: Your train passes near Max Gate, on the train's {side}, the house Thomas Hardy designed for himself. He lived there from 1885 until his death in 1928.

name: Woolbridge Manor
text: Your train passes near Woolbridge Manor, on the train's {side}, a 17th-century house by the old bridge over the River Frome. Its two wall portraits appear in Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles as Tess's ancestors.

name: Bindon Abbey
text: Your train passes near the ruins of Bindon Abbey, on the train's {side}, a Cistercian monastery that moved here in 1172 from its first site near Lulworth Cove, keeping its old name.

name: St Martin's Church, Wareham
text: Your train passes near St Martin's Church in Wareham, on the train's {side}, built in about 1020: the most complete Anglo-Saxon church in Dorset. Inside is a stone effigy of T. E. Lawrence.

name: Royal Naval Cordite Factory, Holton Heath
text: Your train passes near the site of the Royal Naval Cordite Factory, on the train's {side}, set up in the First World War to make cordite for the Navy. Much of it became a nature reserve in 1981.

name: Poole Stadium
text: Your train passes Poole Stadium, on the train's {side}, a speedway track built in the early 1930s to give the town some entertainment during the Great Depression.

name: Scaplen's Court
text: Your train passes near Scaplen's Court, on the train's {side}, a merchant's house of the late 1400s built of Purbeck and Bath stone and cobbles from Poole Quay. It is now a museum.

name: St Aldhelm's Church, Branksome
text: Your train passes near St Aldhelm's Church, on the train's {side}, which began as a Sunday mission to the area's pottery workers in a school room in the 1870s.

name: Bourne Valley Viaducts
text: Your train crosses one of the two Bourne Valley Viaducts over the River Bourne, built in 1888 and 1893; the other is now disused.

name: St Clement's Church, Bournemouth
text: Your train passes St Clement's Church, on the train's {side}, built from 1871 to 1873: the first major church designed by J. D. Sedding, and one of three Grade I listed churches in Bournemouth.

name: Christchurch Castle
text: Your train passes near Christchurch Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman castle by the lowest crossing of the River Avon. The Constable's House beside it, of about 1160, is a rare Norman home.

name: Christchurch Priory
text: Your train passes near Christchurch Priory, on the train's {side}, one of the longest parish churches in the country and as big as many cathedrals.

name: Chewton Glen
text: Your train passes near Chewton Glen, on the train's {side}, now a hotel. Captain Frederick Marryat stayed there in the 1840s while writing The Children of the New Forest.

name: Sway
text: Your train passes Sway, on the train's {side}, which the railway reached in 1888. At the southern edge of the village stands Sway Tower, a concrete folly 66 metres tall built from 1879 to 1885, still the tallest unreinforced concrete structure in the world.

name: New Zealand General Hospital, Brockenhurst
text: Your train passes near the site of a First World War hospital, on the train's {side}, run by New Zealand's army medical corps. It was set up in Brockenhurst in 1916, in two large hotels taken for the purpose.

name: Buckland Rings
text: Your train passes near Buckland Rings, on the train's {side}, an Iron Age hill fort whose banks and ditches can still be clearly seen.

name: Bishop's Dyke
text: Your train crosses Bishop's Dyke, an earthwork round land of the Bishop of Winchester. Legend says King John told the bishop he could have as much land as he could crawl round, and the bishop, who was rather fat, managed a large area.

name: Denny Lodge
text: Your train passes near Denny Lodge, on the train's {side}, the remote building that names a large New Forest parish with no towns, villages, churches or schools.

name: Eling Tide Mill
text: Your train passes near Eling Tide Mill, on the train's {side}, one of only two working tide mills left in the United Kingdom.

name: Redbridge old bridge
text: Your train passes near the old bridge of 1793 at Redbridge, on the train's {side}, at the mouth of the River Test, where merchant ships and Royal Navy ships were built in the 1700s and 1800s.

name: Lymington Lifeboat Station
text: Your train passes near Lymington Lifeboat Station, on the train's {side}, on the west bank of the Lymington River. The RNLI first stationed an inshore lifeboat here in 1965.

name: Army Headquarters
text: Your train passes near Marlborough Lines, on the train's {side}, home of Army Headquarters, the staff who support the head of the British Army.

name: Andover Museum
text: Your train passes near Andover Museum and Museum of the Iron Age, on the train's {side}, in a Georgian town house of the 1750s, with finds from the nearby Danebury hill fort.

name: Laverstoke Mill
text: Your train passes near Laverstoke Mill, on the train's {side}. From the 1720s the Portals made the paper for Bank of England banknotes here; it is now the Bombay Sapphire gin distillery.

name: Milestones Museum
text: Your train passes Milestones Museum, on the train's {side}, where streets of Victorian and 1930s Hampshire have been recreated indoors. It opened in 2000.

name: Basingstoke and Alton Light Railway
text: Your train passes near where the Basingstoke and Alton Light Railway set off, on the train's {side}: opened in 1901, the first English railway built under the Light Railway laws. Its track was taken up in 1917 for use in France.

name: Hyde Abbey
text: Your train passes near the gateway of Hyde Abbey, on the train's {side}, where Alfred the Great, his wife and his son were reburied in 1110. Their remains were lost after the abbey was pulled down in 1538.
